expectation: Cytoplasmic stain filling epithelial/carcinoma cells: lights the epithelial layers (crypts, lining, glands, surface) as connected sheets or rings of cells, and leaves stroma, immune and endothelial cells dark. Common wherever the tissue has epithelium.
notes: Off-tissue haze and broad glowing bands are as bright as the tissue. The ring of epithelial cells in C is not filled with cytoplasmic signal. The bright signals are blobs in the lumen and stroma, and D's brightest 'cell' sits off the tissue. E-cadherin shows no cell structure.
observed: A: yellow haze and bands across the off-tissue background, about as bright as the tissue, which is only faintly tinted. B: haze along tissue texture plus blobs. C: columnar epithelial ring mostly unstained, bright debris in lumen and stroma. D: bright blob off tissue. E: irregular specks; E-cadherin has no structure.
why: The epithelium is not stained cytoplasmically, and the signal is off-tissue haze and debris blobs, not a specific epithelial population.
